# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-5211

# Review — PAN-5211
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — a tail read loses the Codex model, so a bounded conversation's cost becomes $0 and is written to the conversations table (FR-8)

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-5211-review-580b943e
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5211/.pan/review/agent-pan-5211-review-580b943e/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5211 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5211
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/5215
- HEAD reviewed: 580b943ec6c0f5dc93ed90be7708c96eb6e8daa8
- Base: origin/main merge-base a1610f25616 (the local `main` ref is stale; this review diffed against `origin/main...HEAD`, which gives the 50-file manifest set)
- Prior cycle: none (first review of this branch)

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] A tail read zeroes the cost of a bounded Codex conversation and persists the zero — `src/dashboard/server/services/incremental-transcript-reader.ts:186`
- Severity: ! (MUST)
- Classification / requirement scope: specification defect that causes a failure of an explicit in-scope requirement; in_pr_scope. D6 says "Totals stay correct (fact 4)", and fact 4 says the newest `turn_context.model` "repeat[s] every turn, so a tail read keeps the totals correct". That premise is false for real transcripts. FR-8 requires "Cost and token totals still reflect the whole transcript." The plan critic raised this exact gap in round 2 ("Tail reads can zero the cost"), and the PRD lists it under "Unresolved after two critic rounds".
- Trigger and changed-code connection: the new tail read (`incremental-transcript-reader.ts:186`, `start = stats.size > tailReadBytes ? firstLineStartAtOrAfter(...)`) feeds only the last 64 MiB to the accumulator, and so to `createCodexSessionParser`. That parser learns the model only from `turn_context` or `task_started` (`src/lib/cost-parsers/codex-parser.ts:107-113`). With no model it uses `'unknown'`, gets no pricing, and returns `cost: 0` (`codex-parser.ts:141-153`). `getConversationMessagesRead` then calls `updateConversationCost(name, parsed.totalCost, parsed.totalTokens)` because `totalTokens > 0` (`src/lib/overdeck/conversation-reads.ts:644-646`). That runs `UPDATE conversations SET total_cost = ?` (`src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts:873-876`), so the stored cost is overwritten with 0.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected the whole-transcript cost. Observed $0 with the correct token count. Every open of an affected conversation overwrites `conversations.total_cost` with 0, so the conversation list and cost views show $0 for real spend. The accumulator's own comment says this cost exists "so the conversation list shows real spend rather than $0" (`codex-conversation-parser.ts:328-330`).
- Evidence (runtime reproduction against real transcripts, read-only): a scratchpad Vitest probe ran this branch's `createIncrementalTranscriptReader(createCodexConversationAccumulator)` with the default tail read and again with `tailReadBytes: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (whole file):
  - The 227 MiB rollout under `~/.overdeck/agents/conv-20260824-626d/codex-home/` (a managed agent's Codex home): tail cost **0**, whole cost **25.95**, tokens 54,525,887 in both. A read-only `sqlite3` lookup of that name in `~/.overdeck/overdeck.db` returned no row, so I make no claim about its stored cost.
  - `~/.codex/sessions/2026/08/28/rollout-2026-08-28T17-25-43-…` (72 MiB): tail **0**, whole **7.45**.
  - `~/.codex/sessions/2026/08/27/rollout-2026-08-27T09-43-21-…` (69 MiB): tail **0**, whole **6.14**.
  - Control `rollout-2026-09-01T08-33-39-…` (81 MiB, tail has a `turn_context`): 79.45 both ways.
  - A byte scan of all 42 rollouts over 64 MiB on this host found 3 whose last 64 MiB holds no `"type":"turn_context"`. The headline transcript from the issue (`conv-20261110-b6d6`, 1.58 GiB) does have one in its tail, so it is not affected.
  - The NFR-1/NFR-2 test fixture (`codex-transcript-memory.test.ts`) has a single `turn_context` before a 200 MB body, so its tail read also has no model. It asserts only `totalTokens`, which is why CI stays green.
  - Limit: I did not open these conversations in the live dashboard; the write path is a static trace of `conversation-reads.ts:644-646` and `conversations.ts:873-876`.
- Fix: before a tail read starts, recover the newest model record that lies before the tail start. One approach is to scan backward from `start` in blocks for the last `"type":"turn_context"` (or `task_started` with a model) line, then push that one line to the accumulator before the tail lines. A `turn_context` creates no row, so it changes no ids or sequences. Alternatively, pass the model to the cost parser. Then add a `totalCost` assertion (non-zero, equal to a whole-file parse) to the AC-5 tail-read test and to the 200 MB memory test. Also correct the spec: change D6 and fact 4 in `.pan/drafts/PAN-5211.md`, and change the `docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md` bullet "The cost totals stay correct because Codex `token_count` totals are cumulative". That bullet is true for tokens only; cost also needs the model.

## Non-blocking Findings

1. **~ [requirements/spec] At an in-memory boundary the call row is deduplicated away, so the documented outcome does not happen** — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/conversationHistory.ts:137` (unchanged dedupe), `codex-conversation-parser.ts:302-313`. Classification: specification defect (D12 limitation text), whole_feature_scope. This happens after a tail read or a window slide when an output arrives whose call is no longer in memory. The output becomes a stand-alone row whose id is the `call_id`. A later disk page parses the call under the same id, and `prependOlderPage` drops it because that id is already cached. So the call's command and arguments never show. D12 and the docs say both rows show. The trigger is limited to calls that straddle the in-memory start, so the impact is one row per boundary. Fix: give the stand-alone output row a distinct id (for example `codex-tool-out-@<offset>`) while keeping `call_id` lookups for expand. Or correct the D12/docs wording to describe what users actually see. This was critic round 2's "Range boundary hides a tool call".

2. **~ [correctness] Bookmark migration can map a counter id to the wrong message on rare transcripts** — `src/lib/overdeck/codex-bookmark-migration.ts:32-36`. Classification: specification defect / unconfirmed in practice, in_pr_scope. The migration counts legacy ids with a normal windowed accumulator (16 Mi default) plus the 8 MiB oversized-record path. The pre-PR parser had neither limit. The legacy counter then drifts in three cases:
   - When a call is evicted before its output arrives, the output takes the orphan path and adds `sequence += 1`. The old parser matched it with no increment.
   - An oversized message, or an oversized orphan output, becomes a "Skipped" row with no increment. The old parser incremented for it.

   After a drift, every later bookmark is silently rewritten to a neighbouring message. Both triggers are uncommon: a call pending across 4 Mi characters of later rows, or a record over 8 MiB after the scrub. No reproduction was attempted. Fix: count legacy ordinals in a migration-specific pass that mirrors the pre-PR rules (an unbounded call-id set, and oversized records counted by type). This was critic round 2's "Bookmark ordinals drift after eviction".

3. **≉ [correctness] A failed migration is never retried in that process** — `codex-bookmark-migration.ts:62`. `migrated.add(name)` runs before the work. A failed transcript read therefore leaves counter-form bookmarks unresolvable until the next restart. Mappings are collected before any rename, so a read failure writes nothing. Each rename is its own transaction, so a database error partway through leaves the renames partly applied. Fix: add the name to the set after success, and apply all renames in one transaction. This was critic round 2's "Bookmark migration is not atomic or retryable".

4. **? [performance] An unmappable counter bookmark re-streams the whole transcript on every process start** — `codex-bookmark-migration.ts:40-46`. When an id cannot be mapped, `mapCounterIds` reads to EOF. For a 1.6 GB rollout, that is about 0.6 GB of JSON parsed on the main thread on the `GET /bookmarks` path after each restart. It yields between 1 MiB chunks, so it does not freeze the event loop, but it delays the bookmark list. Clicking such a bookmark in a bounded conversation also makes `loadOlderUntil` page back through every disk page to byte 0. Impact is unmeasured. Consider recording "attempted" ids persistently, or running the scan in the worker lane. I checked for other stores of Codex message ids (`conversation-message-resolver.ts` computes ids at query time; the jev turn-end store is in memory and not persisted) and found no other consumer that the id change breaks.

5. **? [correctness] The stricter WS resume applies to every harness** — `src/dashboard/server/services/conversation/window.ts:189-193`. `holdsAfterRow` turns any resume whose newest client sequence the server no longer holds into a windowed reset. The Claude parser assigns stable line sequences (`conversation/parser.ts:198`) and the frontend creates no sequenced rows (`resumePayloadFromCache` uses server rows only), so I found no current regression. The worst case is an extra reset that drops paged-in older rows.

6. **? [requirements] A record over `RECORD_FULL_READ_MAX_BYTES` stays `bodyOmitted` with no `result` after expand** — `codex-transcript-ranges.ts:51`. The loaded entry has no body to show. This needs a scrubbed record over 64 MiB, so it is hypothetical.

7. **Note:** AC-8's text ("ids stay counter-form from byte 0") contradicts D7 as revised after critique round 1 (offset ids for every located parse). The code follows D7, which is the newer decision. The AC text should be updated.

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** the blocker, plus advisories 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Verified as correct: the line splitter's offsets across chunk boundaries and the `flushComplete` no-newline case; the absolute call index across slides; `result()` copies its arrays, so slides do not change earlier snapshots; a previously cached entry over the cap is removed (`cache.delete(file)` runs before the re-check); disk paging always moves its cursor back.
- **Security:** no new trust boundary. `seq` is validated as a safe non-negative integer, `findCodexToolEntryFrom` checks the bounds and the line start, and the transcript path is resolved by the server. Images are scrubbed on every serve path (expand, disk page, migration). `toolResultLocations` and `historyStartOffset` are removed from the agent body, the subagent body and every window. No issue found.
- **Performance:** reads are async (`fs/promises`) with no `execSync`. A disk page parses at most 8+16+32+64 MiB in the worst case. The memory guard test passes on CI. The only finding is advisory 4.
- **Requirements/UX:** FR-8 is unmet (blocker). The others are listed below.

## Scope Note
- During this review another agent edited this worktree. After 19:19 there are uncommitted changes to `incremental-transcript-reader.ts` (a `tailContextMarker` back-scan that looks like a fix for the blocker), `codex-conversation-parser.ts`, `codex-transcript-ranges.ts`, `codex-incremental-parser.test.ts` and the xBRIEF. This review covers only committed HEAD 580b943e. Those edits were not reviewed and must be committed and pushed before the next cycle can evaluate them. My probes wrote only to the session scratchpad.
- The integration points were traced at HEAD. `getCachedMessages` returns the Codex reader result unreshaped (`conversation-reads.ts:281-282`). The worker's `parseTranscriptSnapshot` returns the parser result as-is (`dashboard-db-task.ts:328-333`). `full-parse-stream.ts:60` passes the raw parse result into `createTranscriptDelta`. So `historyStartOffset`, `toolResultLocations` and `bounded` reach the HTTP, agent and WS entry points.
- All four "blocks-the-design" items from critique round 2 shipped unresolved. Three are advisory here because their triggers are narrow. The cost one is reproducible on real transcripts on this host, so it blocks.
